subject: health

location.unitTitle: Mental Health, Stress, and Support Networks

standards: Michigan Health: Mental and Emotional Health
instructions: Complete the private-safe task without disclosing medical history, diagnosis, body measurements, or sexual history.
Use a fictional scenario when offered and identify a trusted adult or qualified professional where appropriate.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain stress and coping in your own words and give or identify a valid example.
Use a diagram, model, quotation, data display, map, demonstration, or worked process to show understanding of anxiety and depression literacy without diagnosis.
Apply protective factors in a new realistic situation. Show the process or cite evidence.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, unsafe choice, or design flaw involving supporting a peer without becoming the counselor; correct it and explain why.
Connect stress and coping with help-seeking plans. Explain how the ideas support, constrain, contrast with, or build on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit project: Respond to fictional situations with boundaries, coping options, trusted support, and urgent escalation when indicated.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy or quality, and one next question.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated accuracy or fidelity criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated evidence and reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated application or performance criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated checking and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Mental Health, Stress, and Support Networks?
